newsitem.title: UK: British food exports up 1 pct in 1996, grains star.
newsitem.headline: British food exports up 1 pct in 1996, grains star.

text.p: British food and drink exports rose to 10.1 billion sterling in 1996, up by one per cent on 1995, according to Food From Britain.
"The cereals sector was a star performer," Food From Britain, which is a marketing consultancy funded by industry and government to promote food exports, said in a statement.
The total value of cereal exports rose by 20 per cent to 1.6 billion sterling, it said.
"Breakfast cereals, cakes, biscuits and bread all performed exceptionally well."

According to the 1996 figures, around three million tonnes of cereals are exported in cereal-based foods which, when added to 5,580,000 tonnes of exported unmilled grain, means that around half the total British cereal crop is exported, Food From Britain said.
The rise in exports is despite the effects of nine months of the ban on beef exports, which was imposed on March 20, 1996, it said. Beef exports were worth 600 million stg in 1995, it said.
